pr_title: Add debugging attributes to System.Security.Claims types
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/86421

After changes:

![image](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/assets/303201/5ad628c0-5d68-48ef-b434-f92b6bb8cdeb)

I have a question about `DebuggerDisplayAttribute` and ref assemblies. I added them to the implementation classes and ran the ref update command - `dotnet msbuild /t:GenerateReferenceAssemblySource` - but they weren't added to the reference file. I had to do it manually. What should I do here?

Extra work: It's worth adding debugger proxy views for `ClaimsPrincipal` and `ClaimsIdentity`. The proxy can remove the private/internal fields and display the counts from the claims collections. Proxies are more work so I'll hold off on that for now.

Thoughts so far?

**Update:**

With type proxies:

**ClaimsPrincipal:**

![image](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/assets/303201/d54e9e6e-2ef6-4bdb-be9d-40e88b34a4ff)

**ClaimsIdentity:**

![image](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/assets/303201/956972dc-c031-434e-89f9-9d785b001e56)

> I have a question about `DebuggerDisplayAttribute` and ref assemblies. I added them to the implementation classes and ran the ref update command - `dotnet msbuild /t:GenerateReferenceAssemblySource` - but they weren't added to the reference file. I had to do it manually. What should I do here?

cc @ViktorHofer

> I have a question about DebuggerDisplayAttribute and ref assemblies. I added them to the implementation classes and ran the ref update command - dotnet msbuild /t:GenerateReferenceAssemblySource - but they weren't added to the reference file. I had to do it manually. What should I do here?

DebuggerDisplay is not part of the API contract.  It's an implementation detail found via reflection by tools at execution time, and thus they're only relevant to the implementation assemblies.  The genapi tool is told not to add them to ref assemblies:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/2f18df4291febc514781ecf92593d9d00f3d8f57/eng/DefaultGenApiDocIds.txt#L12
Thanks. Yes, I just tested removing them, and for some reason now the attributes work without being in the ref. I'm not sure what I did wrong before.
I just added type proxies. Original issue updated with screenshots.

"runtime (Build ios-arm64 Release AllSubsets_Mono)" is failing. It seems unrelated.

Can I merge? Should I rebase to try to get a green build?

issue_context.title: Improve debugging experience of ClaimsPrincipal
issue_context.body:
In ASP.NET Core we're trying to [improve the debug experience of HttpContext](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/48205). One of the properties on HttpContext is the current user, represented by `ClaimsPrincipal`. Today it has a relatively standard debug experience. You can see it below in screenshots. A couple of debugger display attributes should make it easier to see important information at a glance.

**ClaimsIdentity:**

![image](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/assets/303201/03c9eb96-d38a-47aa-8d79-94a12ed9a9c1)

Debugger could display `"Name: {Name}, IsAuthenticated: {IsAuthenticated}, Claims count: {Claims.Count}"`

**ClaimsPrincipal:**

![image](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/assets/303201/9b48fa73-a9c1-412b-8d70-8e6fca390c70)

The usual case for a `ClaimsPrincipal` is one primary identity. In that case, it could just display information about that identity: `"Identity name: {Identity.Name}, IsAuthenticated: {Identity.IsAuthenticated}, Claims count: {Identity.Claims.Count}"`

If `ClaimsPrincipal` has multiple identities, then it could display more general information: `"Identity count: {Identities.Count}, Claims count: {Claims.Count}"`.

Also, the [`Claims` property](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8c637de325578398894d482f4855d0db4af78dbb/src/libraries/System.Security.Claims/src/System/Security/Claims/ClaimsPrincipal.cs#L223-L238) should show the count. How do you customize the debug display of a yield enumerable method? Can you add a debugger display attribute to a property?

**Claim**:

![image](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/assets/303201/0802fdbd-0290-48e7-854a-60c67dd171da)

`Claim` has a [ToString()](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8c637de325578398894d482f4855d0db4af78dbb/src/libraries/System.Security.Claims/src/System/Security/Claims/Claim.cs#L510-L520) already and looks good in the debugger.

review_comments: What are the benefits of using custom `[DebuggerTypeProxy]` in this particular example? Showing only selected properties?

It shows only public properties (no internal or protected).

Also, in a real edge case situation, if someone overrode the `Claims` collection to return a type that doesn't have a debug-friendly view then it would still use the debug view of `List<Claims>`.

The identity proxy isn't useful as the other principal proxy because the claims collection count is already displayed. It's a slightly nicer experience, but I can remove it if you'd like.
